sentence: This project studies how an iris can be reprogrammed into a lens to model how eye tissue regenerates in vertebrates.
This project runs a shared lab facility that supports research on brain injury and on recovery and repair of the brain.
This project tries to find out what starts neurological damage when the body has too little thiamine.
This project sets up shared instrumentation and expert services that support biomedical, clinical, behavioral and community research.
This project builds a system that measures iron oxide nanoparticles in rat kidneys that have been cryopreserved for transplantation.
This project studies how the X-chromosome affects Alzheimer's disease and why women are more likely than men to develop it.
This project provides mouse models and related services to the scientific community.
This project collects cancer epitope data and builds tools to analyze and predict from it for the research community.
This project builds computer tools that help researchers analyze data from single-cell genomic technologies.
This project studies how genes downstream of master regulator genes control intestinal stem cells in the fruit fly Drosophila melanogaster.
This project studies a treatment that targets lactate metabolism and combines metformin to slow tumor cell growth linked to diabetes.
This project develops and tests a way to detect cirrhosis, or liver scarring, using electronic health data.
This project improves protease inhibitors against a viral protease to make preclinical drug candidates for antiviral treatment.
This project studies how signaling that triggers cell death and interferon production is controlled differently in different cell types.
This project uses sequencing and protein analysis to study how the immune response to Ebola virus changes cells.
This project provides patient-derived xenograft models and cell lines to help find molecular drivers of prostate cancer lineage plasticity.
This project uses zebrafish to study how a retinoid transporter protein affects retinoid signaling and the survival of cells in the eye.
This project builds a human vein-chip model to predict and test treatments for neointimal hyperplasia, a scarring process in vein grafts.
This project studies how inhibition changes the immune microenvironment and response to immune checkpoint blockade in small cell lung cancer.
This project provides cell analysis methods such as flow cytometry and single cell gene expression to study inflammatory rheumatic diseases.
